title: Internal Resource Matrix and Access Mapping: Onboarding to Impact
author: Maya Patel
body:
Purpose

This playbook maps the core internal resources, access patterns, and ownerships that enable new and existing Redwoood employees to get to impact quickly. It unifies onboarding checklists, the career lattice touchpoints (growth milestones and tooling), and benefits entry points into a single, searchable reference for managers, people-ops partners, and ICs.

Audience

- New hires (first 90 days)
- Managers onboarding new team members
- People-ops and IT support engineers
- Team leads who own role competency reviews

Principles

1. Fast first-principle access: 50% of new hires should be able to run useful work within 3 business days.
2. Least-privilege by default: grant minimal permissions during ramp; escalate on demonstrated need.
3. Ownership clarity: every resource has a named owner and a documented escalation path.
4. Single source of truth: this doc points to canonical onboarding artifacts and tool-runbooks.

Quick glossary

- Access groups: predefined role-based collections in our IAM (e.g., infra-dev, eng-readonly, hr-admin).
- Tool registry: central catalog of internal apps with SSO and provisioning instructions.
- Career lattice: rubric that maps competencies to promotion signals and available learning paths.

Onboarding checklist (manager + new-hire) — 0–10 days

1. Day 0 (People-ops): create account skeleton, send welcome email, schedule orientation.
2. Day 0–1 (IT): grant baseline SSO groups: company-sso, corp-network, slack-basic.
3. Day 1 (Manager): assign 30/60/90 goals in GrowthLoom and add to team roster.
4. Day 1–3 (Manager + New hire): request role-specific access via Access Portal (see table below).
5. By Day 3: confirm access to code repo (git/redwood), dev cluster (if applicable), and CI build logs.
6. By Day 10: complete first shadow session and knowledge-transfer with buddy.

Role-based Access Matrix (common roles)

| Role | Typical tool access | Initial groups provisioned | Escalation owner | Time-to-expected-access |
|------|--------------------|--------------------------|------------------|-------------------------|
| Backend engineer | git/redwood, CI, staging GPU pool dashboard, Datadog traces | eng-basic, infra-dev-request | infra-platform@redwood.com | 1–3 business days |
| ML engineer | model-store, GPU fleet console, experiment tracker, S3 buckets | eng-basic, ml-experiments | ml-platform@redwood.com | 2–4 business days |
| SRE/on-call | PagerDuty, runbook-console, k8s-read/write, capacity dashboards | eng-sre, ops-oncall | sre-team@redwood.com | 1 business day (oncall shadow longer) |
| Product manager | Analytics dashboards, roadmap board, customer CRM (read), feature flags | go-to-market, pm-view | product-ops@redwood.com | same day |
| People-ops / HR | HRIS, payroll, benefits admin, access portal admin | hr-admin | people-ops@redwood.com | same day |

Notes: for dedicated GPU pool access we require manager approval (Access Portal workflow) and a signed GPU usage policy. New hires requiring on-prem access need network onboarding (VM/VPN provisioning) which adds 2–5 days.

Promotion and career-lattice touchpoints

- Growth signals tracked in GrowthLoom: impact outcomes, mentorship contributions, reliability metrics (for infra roles), and product outcomes.
- Competency review cadence: 6-month check-ins with formal calibration every 12 months.
- Promotion packet checklist: role summary, 3x peer feedback, 2x manager write-ups, and 6–12 month work artifacts.

Example competency-to-access mapping (milestones)

- IC2 -> IC3 (mid): demonstrates ownership of a service, can request elevated access (infra-change role) after paired review.
- IC3 -> IC4 (senior): expected to contribute to architecture ADRs; granted broader read access and ability to open feature branches in protected repos.

Benefits entry points and who to contact

- Health & benefits enrollment: first 30 days; contact benefits@redwood.com or people-ops portal.
- Remote stipend and home office equipment requests: submit through Internal Tools > Equipment Request. Manager approval required.
- Wellness and therapy stipend: submit receipts to finance+benefits and see reimbursement policy (Finance runbook).

Internal tools registry (sample entries)

- GrowthLoom: career and goal-tracking tool. Owner: people-ops. Onboarding runbook: /runbooks/growthloom-setup.
- Access Portal: central IAM request system. Owner: infra-platform. CLI: accessctl request --role <role>.
- Dev cluster console: GPU and staging environment dashboard. Owner: ml-platform. Requires infra-dev-request group.
- Oncall console (PagerDuty): SRE team-owned; see runbook /runbooks/oncall-rotation.

Provisioning workflow (Access Portal)

1. Manager selects role template and submits request in Access Portal.
2. Automated checks run (manager tenure, role seniority, background checks).
3. Access is provisioned to a temporary token for 14 days to allow safe incremental validation.
4. After 14 days manager confirms continued need; access becomes permanent and added to monthly IAM report.

Tool-specific runbook examples (excerpt)

- Granting repo access
  1. Open Access Portal > Repos > Request git/redwood access.
  2. Select team and manager approval.
  3. CI will run a membership sync within 15 minutes; notify new hire when complete.

- Requesting GPU pool quota (ML engineers)
  1. File a quota request with ml-platform including expected workload, test dataset size, and duration.
  2. Include cost center code and manager approval.
  3. ml-platform will respond with schedule for reservation (48–72 hours typical).

Manager checklist for first 90 days (owner: manager)

- Week 1: 1:1 every day (shadowing, tool walkthroughs), confirm access matrix completed.
- Week 2–4: assign first micro-project with clear success metrics (latency regression test, feature prototype, doc update).
- Month 2: mid-ramp review (skills, access changes, buddy feedback).
- Month 3: impact review and calibration readout with people-ops.

FAQ (short)

Q: If a new hire needs expedited access for a customer incident, what do we do?
A: Manager files an "expedite" in Access Portal with incident ID; infra-platform has a 4-hour SLA for expedited approvals during business hours.

Q: Who approves promotion packets?
A: Direct manager submits packet; final sign-off after calibration by People-ops + peer calibration committee.

Ownership and contacts

- People-ops (Maya Patel) — onboarding programs, career lattice, promotion coordination.
- Infra-platform (Carlos Mendes) — Access Portal, IAM, provisioning.
- ML-platform (Priya Rao) — GPU pools, model infra access.
- Finance & Benefits (Elena Fischer) — benefits, reimbursements, wellness programs.

Change log

How to request updates

Submit a doc update request to people-ops@redwood.com with the section name and justification. For access changes, open an infra-platform ticket with audit justification.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets

- Quick check group membership (internal CLI): rc-cli iam whoami --groups
- Request temporary infra change role: accessctl request --role infra-change --duration 14d --reason "paired-release"
